NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are

  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 28, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Fire Department Community Services Liaison Kaelyn Floyd.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald M. Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/PW Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Public Works Manager Kirsten Graham
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2026 "WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN proclaimed May 2026 as “Wildfire Preparedness Month,” and presented
the Proclamation to Los Angeles County Fire Department Community Services Liaison Kaelyn
Floyd, who announced the upcoming annual brush clearance inspections as well as the
upcoming Fire Service Day at Fire Station 106 on May 9.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2026 "OLDER AMERICANS MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN proclaimed May 2026 as “Older Americans Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS
  BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MARCH & APRIL 2026

  APPROVED WARRANTS 69436 THROUGH 69617 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $2,154,155.50; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 030426 THROUGH
  030526; 040126 THROUGH 040526; IN THE AMOUNT OF $345,804.37 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $2,499,959.87 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF MARCH 2026
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 28, 2026
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF MARCH 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 6, 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 8, 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 14, 2026

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

H.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 15, 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 761 - AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 13.08 (SEWER SERVICE SYSTEM) OF THE ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council hold the second reading and adopt proposed
  Ordinance No. 761 amending and restating Municipal Code Chapter 13.08 (Sewer
  Service System).

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT PROPOSED ORDINANCE NO. 761 AMENDING AND RESTATING
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 13.08 (SEWER SERVICE SYSTEM).

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 761 by title.

B.  REQUEST TO ENTER INTO AN AMENDED “MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT
  MULTI-YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM” WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 28, 2026
   Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute an
  amendment to the Measure M Funding Agreement (Amendment No. 2) Multi-Year
  Sub Regional Program, with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA), in the grand total amount of $4,480,252.

Public Works Manager Graham provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT (AMENDMENT NO. 2) MULTI-YEAR
  SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM, WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA), IN THE
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $4,480,252.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PERSONNEL RESOLUTION UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2621 amending the
  City’s authorized position plan to authorize one Accountant position to support an
  upcoming transition within the Administrative Services Department, and to remove
  two part-time Office Assistant positions and add one full-time Office Assistant position
  to align staffing with current operational needs and maintain continuity in
  administrative support functions.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that previously, two part-time positions ensured
coverage for the front office. However, following the City Hall remodel, the more open layout
now allows multiple staff members to assist with front office coverage for the public, in
response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2621 AMENDING THE CITY’S AUTHORIZED
  POSITION PLAN TO AUTHORIZE ONE ACCOUNTANT POSITION TO
  SUPPORT AN UPCOMING TRANSITION WITHIN THE ADMINISTRATIVE
  SERVICES DEPARTMENT, AND TO REMOVE TWO PART-TIME OFFICE
  ASSISTANT POSITIONS AND ADD ONE FULL-TIME OFFICE ASSISTANT
  POSITION TO ALIGN STAFFING WITH CURRENT OPERATIONAL NEEDS
  AND MAINTAIN CONTINUITY IN ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FUNCTIONS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2621 by title.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 28, 2026
 10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA will be attending the first meeting of the South Bay Housing
Trust this Thursday, as well as Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority Board meeting
tomorrow night.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER announced that COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA was
elected as Chair of Palos Verdes Transit Authority Board at the last meeting.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN attended the Los Angeles County Sanitation District Board meeting last
week.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  MAYORAL ROTATION POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the proposed Policy, suggest any
  revisions, and approve the Policy (as it may be revised).

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA and HUFF stated they are in favor of the policy change, with
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noting that most people elected to Council have previous public
service experience on the City’s Commissions and Committees.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPTED THE PROPOSED MAYORAL ROTATION POLICY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting at 7:29 p.m. to Tuesday, May 12, 2026, at 7:00
p.m. for the purpose of a regular City Council meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Frank V. Zerunyan, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 28, 2026
